slides.title: Git already fingerprints every file; we use that as the cache key

columns.heading: The mechanism
items: Each file's blob SHA keys its parsed facts; an unchanged file is never parsed twice, across branches and commits
Entities and edges are rows under the exact commit, so 'on RIL prod' and 'on UAT' are different, exact questions
A new commit inserts; it never updates or deletes older rows. History is what remains
config/refs.json lists nine refs; the other ~2,100 branches never enter the graph
10,658 source blobs (2.17 M lines) are stored in Postgres, so answering needs no clone

columns.heading: What it buys
items: 96% cache hit on backfill; a full re-index of the backend in 1.65 s
28,352 file instances across 14 commits collapse to 11,020 distinct blobs
secrets paths are dropped before any read; the model's DB role is SELECT-only
shared endpoint nodes connect a dashboard call to the Rails action that serves it, no resolver pass needed

slides.title: Nine deployed branches, each answerable on its own
rows: supplier app; no screen layer yet
slides.note: Five older dashboard branches were removed from the graph this week at the team's request. Adding a branch is a config edit plus one indexing run.

slides.title: What stops the agent from making things up

items.text: Any file path the model names that was not in its facts is replaced before display
'The graph does not show…' is a first-class answer; unresolved hops are listed, never hidden
Complete result sets are rendered as tables; the prose may only summarise them
Workflow diagram steps must reference facts the model was given, or they are dropped
Triage verdicts are limited to the set the facts allow; others are downgraded
Every answer ends with the exact commits it was read from
Eval: 7 of 7 scored questions cite a real file, invent no path and name the branch
5 of 5 saved CS answers contain zero code names, paths or code events
Path guard applies to plan and triage answers; the sub-second guided path relies on its narrower prompt
No judge-based scoring of answer quality yet; the eval checks honesty properties, not correctness
Neither tests nor eval run in CI

slides.note: Honesty properties are properties of the code path, so they hold for any model behind the gateway.

slides.title: Conversations are personal, replayable and understood in context

columns.heading: Built
items: Every turn is stored with its event stream gzipped (4.4× smaller measured); reopening redraws prose, trace, tables, template and diagram exactly
'And for Reliance?' is rewritten into a standalone question from the last six turns, at minimal model effort; the person sees 'understood as'
The writer is told the conversation may explain what the person means, never serve as a fact
Replay events are pruned after 180 days; question and answer text stay
A saved answer is a snapshot; one click re-runs it against today's data

slides.title: Per-customer configuration and ticket triage

cards.title: What is on for Reliance?
body: Resolves a customer's switches exactly as the platform does: default ← company master ← active override (rule taken from the Rails model)
435 global switches, 19,544 active overrides across 16,291 companies
Names repeat (two 'RELIANCE INDUSTRIES LIMITED'), so company ids are always shown and agreement vs difference is separated
Reverse direction: which companies have X on, with the same precedence

cards.title: Ticket triage
body: Paste a complaint → customer, likely feature with confidence, governing switches with effective values, guides, screens, owners from commit history
Verdict: CS can resolve · needs a config change · needs engineering · need more information
The verdict is chosen only from the set the facts allow; a switch at its default proves nothing
Accuracy unmeasured: 3 written examples (2 of 3 as expected); needs 20 real anonymised tickets; HubSpot lookup not built

slides.note: Both read the UAT mirror; production values must be confirmed until a production replica exists.

slides.title: One VM: the agent deploys on merge, the graph is still indexed by hand

items.text: GCP VM (Debian, Postgres 17 + pgvector, nginx → Node service) with systemd units for the agent and the live poller
Merge to main deploys the agent: pull, build, migrate, restart, health check, roll back on failure (WIF + IAP, no keys)
67 tests in 17 files pass; migrations 001–019 chained in one command
Bootstrap database dump in the repo; teammate runbooks for VM load and update
Business documents in the repo are re-ingested on every deploy
Push-model indexing on merge (bundle → HMAC endpoint → index, embed, gc) is built and documented but has not indexed anything yet
VM indexing of new commits is still a manual command; so is embedding after it
No monitoring, alerting or scheduled backups; chat backup is a documented command
Tests and eval do not run in CI
Runtime call evidence needs a tracer harness that lives outside this repo

slides.title: Six questions, one story

columns.heading: As Customer Success
items: "Which master configs are on by default?" → complete table of 78 rows, plain-English summary
"And which of those are switched off for Reliance?" → understood as a standalone question; per-company effective values with ids
"Walk me through the buyer journey from a purchase request to the PO" → screens and clicks from the code, workflow diagram beside it
Paste a ticket → triage card: customer, feature, switches, guide, owner, verdict

columns.heading: As Engineer
items: "What happens when GET /activity_logs is called?" → controller, serializer, files and lines, trace graph
"Show me the RFQ Template - Materials used by GMMCO" → the template drawn as the platform draws it, columns and price components
sign out and sign in as CS to show the same template question with no code anywhere

slides.note: Every demo answer is reproducible on the laptop; latency is 5–15 s for plain questions and 15–30 s for technical ones when the gateway is healthy.

slides.title: What does not exist yet
slides.subtitle: Two slides of gaps, ordered by how much they limit the answers, each verified by reading the code and the database on 16 September.

slides.title: What the graph cannot see or do today

items.text: Production data: every live value is UAT; a production read replica does not exist
Front-end parser is regex based: 31.6% of API call sites unresolved; a Babel-based extractor is the fix
Redux/state layer, component tree, background jobs, config-key reads and model→table edges have no extractor
Backend production branch is still the bootstrap import; FEATURE, PERSON and OWNS layers are not re-derived by the indexer
Runtime 'A actually calls B' evidence cannot be refreshed for new commits
Supplier app (web-bidding) has no screen layer
Zero PRDs attached to commits; the PR-body ingestion job and the PR template are not adopted
16 uploaded guides; the journeys people ask about need about fifty; none of them link to code by identifier yet
Notion, Drive and Confluence connectors; no upload button in the UI
Indexing on merge is not live; the VM graph lags until someone runs a command
No alert when the mirror or the graph goes stale

slides.title: What users will notice, and what a reviewer should

items.text: HubSpot: no ticket lookup by number, no write-back; triage is paste-only
Template preview is our drawing with the platform's measurements, not the dashboard's own renderer
Workflow diagrams are model-authored then validated; no deterministic diagram from graph data alone
No Slack or Teams entry point; no shared chat links; no admin UI for accounts and roles
No self-service password reset; Google SSO removed until a hostname with TLS exists
Triage accuracy unmeasured; feedback votes are stored but nothing reads them yet
Eval covers 8 engineer questions and honesty only; no CS, template, config or follow-up cases; no CI gate
Answer quality depends on FAST_SMALLER through a gateway that stalls; the fallback covers stalls, not quality
Fixed this week: the model's SQL role could read chats and sessions; revoked in migration 019
Saved-chat replay is not re-filtered when a role changes; the final summary event is unfiltered

slides.note: Everything on these two slides was found by auditing the repository and database, not by recollection.
